correctness.rationale: On the common test core the compositions give the positive kernel (y^beta-x^beta)(x-y)^(alpha-1)/Gamma(alpha) on y<x. Squaring and putting y=xz gives x^(2(alpha+beta)-1) times the z integral; its endpoints have orders z^(2beta) and (1-z)^(2alpha). This yields the supercritical Hilbert–Schmidt norm and density gives uniqueness. Below the line, unit-norm dilations supported in a scaled compact subinterval have output norm on a scaled interval to their right bounded below by c epsilon^(alpha+beta), so there is no bounded extension. At alpha+beta=0 the logarithmic unitary conjugates the kernel to the positive right-translation average with density h(s)=(exp(alpha s)-1)exp(-s/2)(1-exp(-s))^(alpha-1)/Gamma(alpha). Its finite mass bounds the norm; normalized long plateaus asymptotically realize the mass by restricting the s integration to [0,R] and then sending the plateau length and R to infinity in that order. Translating the plateaus away from zero makes them weakly null without losing this lower bound, proving essential norm equality. For any nonzero g the translation norm decreases on a positive-measure set of s because of lost mass on [0,s], proving nonattainment under the strictly positive density. Substitution z=exp(-s) evaluates the mass as the stated positive difference of beta integrals divided by Gamma(alpha). Finally, with j(z)=(z^(-alpha)-1)^2(1-z)^(2alpha-2), the exact truncated energy is Gamma(alpha)^(-2) times the integral from epsilon to 1 of j(z) log(z/epsilon). Both j and |log z|j are integrable, giving the stated cutoff coefficient and bounded remainder. The same coefficient arises by dominated convergence of the Hilbert–Schmidt numerator as beta tends to -alpha from above.

originality.rationale: After comparing ordinary and weighted fractional integrals, power commutators and fractional Volterra boundary laws, the supported distinct claim is the concrete singular-power commutator trichotomy with exact operator and essential norms on the critical line and the common Hilbert–Schmidt coefficient. The tools of one-sided convolution, homogeneity, and beta integration are not claimed as new. Older weighted commutator literature is materially relevant but no verified coverage of this exact bundle was found; the named access limitations remain.

value.rationale: The singular power multiplier creates a natural homogeneity boundary where compactness disappears but boundedness survives. The simultaneous sharp norm, nonattainment, and agreement of the energy divergence under parameter approach and spatial cutoff give quantitative information that a weighted boundedness estimate alone would miss. The proof explains the agreement through the same remaining ratio integral, rather than through unrelated numerical fits.
residual_risks: No S_p law beyond S_2, other L^p spaces, or endpoint half-orders are inferred.
